channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tashkent recognizes property rights for an additional 525 citizens
item.description: Tashkent has officially recognized the property rights of an additional 525 citizens for individual housing and land plots. This brings the total number of citizens whose rights have been recognized to 927, facilitating the legalization of informally occupied properties.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japan strengthen energy cooperation, discuss new projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's Energy Minister met with Japan's State Minister of Economy, Trade, and Industry to discuss expanding bilateral energy cooperation. They reviewed ongoing projects in generation, transmission, and gas infrastructure modernization, and agreed to support existing and new initiatives.

item.title: Uzbekistan's international reserves surpass $72 billion, gold holdings hit record high
item.description: Uzbekistan's international reserves grew by $7.78 billion in August, reaching $72.13 billion by September 1. Gold reserves hit a record 438.9 tons, with their value increasing to $64.93 billion due to rising global gold prices and central bank purchases. Foreign currency assets decreased, while securities saw a slight increase.

item.title: NATO Thwarts Russian Secret Arctic Operation Near Svalbard
item.description: NATO forces from the US, UK, and Norway have stopped Russian submarines near the Svalbard archipelago. The submarines were reportedly attempting to test a new weapon designed to disable global internet cables.

item.title: Tashkent Proposes Raising Bus and Metro Fares to 2,500 Som
item.description: A draft document released for public discussion in Tashkent proposes increasing bus and metro fares starting October 1. The proposed fare is 2,500 som for electronic payments and 3,000 som for cash. Discounted tariffs will apply to transport cards.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish Commission for Cultural Property Repatriation
item.description: Uzbekistan will form a commission to systematically search for, legally protect, and return cultural assets taken abroad. The commission, operating under the President, aims to recover stolen heritage.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Utilize Over 46,000 First-Floor Apartments for Business
item.description: Over 46,000 first-floor apartments in Uzbekistan can be used for trade and services without reclassifying them as non-residential property. This initiative is expected to create jobs and boost incomes, according to the Construction Ministry.

item.title: Leaders Not Understanding Current Politics Will Be Dismissed, Says Mirziyoyev
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev warned leaders that poverty reduction efforts must go beyond meetings and reports. He criticized officials sent from Tashkent for staying in offices instead of visiting neighborhoods to understand the real situation and guide local authorities.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves Alphabet Changes, Adopting 28 Latin-Based Letters
item.description: The Uzbek Senate has approved amendments to the law on the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet. The new alphabet will feature 28 letters and an apostrophe, replacing the current 26 letters and three letter combinations. Documents and currency issued under the old alphabet will remain valid during the transition period.

item.title: Tajikistan authorities recruit citizens for work in Turkey and Russia
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Employment Agency is recruiting citizens for jobs in Turkey and Russia. Positions include skilled labor, drivers, and construction workers. Salaries range from $700-$1250 in Turkey and 80,000-140,000 rubles in Russia.

item.title: Environmental inspector dies in Sirdaryo while stopping illegal fishing
item.description: An environmental inspector in Sirdaryo died while attempting to stop individuals engaged in illegal fishing with electric nets. The inspector fell into the water during the confrontation and his body was recovered the next day. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Tajik teenager faces criminal charges for allegedly stabbing another minor in Badakhshan
item.description: Tajikistan's Interior Ministry reported that a criminal case has been opened against a 15-year-old boy in Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region suspected of stabbing another minor. The incident occurred on September 7 near the "Chorbogh" park in Khorugh, where the suspect allegedly attacked a 14-year-old with a knife.

item.title: Pakistan warns Iran to restrain Houthis, conveys Saudi message
item.description: Pakistan has warned Iran to restrain the Houthi group and conveyed an official message from Saudi Arabia. This measure is being taken to prevent the escalation of the conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Tajik businessman admits sending sanctioned equipment to Russia in US court
item.description: A Tajik businessman has admitted in a US court to sending sanctioned equipment to Russia. The details of the case and the specific equipment involved were not immediately disclosed.

item.title: Tajik businessman arrested in US for sanctions violations against Russia has been released
item.description: Salimjon Nasriddinov, a Tajik businessman detained in the US nearly three years ago for allegedly sending sanctioned equipment to Russia, has been released. His family declined to provide further details, and the terms of his release are unknown. Nasriddinov had pleaded guilty to the charges in a New York federal court.

item.title: Expert discusses German election results and the rise of the AfD party
item.description: An expert analyzes the recent German federal state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right AfD party secured a significant victory with 43.8% of the vote. The article discusses potential coalition scenarios and the implications of the AfD's growing influence on Germany's party system, noting the traditional refusal of major parties to cooperate with the far-right.

item.title: Ecological police officer killed in the line of duty confronting illegal fishing
item.description: An ecological police inspector died while on duty after confronting individuals engaged in illegal fishing using electric seines. The incident occurred when the inspector encountered the offenders resisting his attempts to stop their activity. Further details were not immediately available.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Benefits and Preferences for Entrepreneurs
item.description: A seminar in Surkhandarya discussed a presidential decree offering new benefits for entrepreneurs, including a three-year exemption from inspections for small businesses. The decree aims to reduce state interference and strengthen protections for businesses, fostering economic growth.

item.title: Foreign national detained at Osh airport for alleged cigarette smuggling
item.description: A foreign national was detained at Osh International Airport on suspicion of smuggling Esse Change cigarettes. The State Committee for National Security reported the operation involved customs officers. A criminal case for economic smuggling has been opened, and the damage to the state budget is being determined.

item.title: Tajik company Ayan Capital raises $100 million in London
item.description: Tajik company Ayan Capital has reportedly raised approximately $100 million in London. The company was founded in London by co-founders of "Alif."

item.title: Kamchybek Tashiev's defense to appeal Bishkek court ruling in 'Letter of 75' case
item.description: The defense team for former State Committee for National Security Chairman Kamchybek Tashiev plans to appeal the Bishkek City Court's decision in the 'Letter of 75' case. His lawyer called the ruling illegal and unfounded, citing a reclassification of charges.

item.title: CIS Interpol Bureaus Discuss Cooperation Development in Minsk
item.description: Heads of national Interpol bureaus from CIS member states met in Minsk to discuss cooperation. Delegations from Azerbaijan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, UAE, and Uzbekistan attended. The meeting focused on information exchange, existing problems, and solutions for enhancing regional law enforcement collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan disburses over 285 million soms for 'Bala Yrysy' child benefit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has financed another payment of the 'Bala Yrysy' child benefit, totaling 285.59 million soms. The Ministry of Labor reported that 232,229 recipients are now included after database updates. This is an increase of over 40,000 recipients and nearly 50 million soms compared to July's payments.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan court reclassifies charges in 'Letter of 75' case, imposes probation
item.description: The Bishkek City Court reclassified charges in the 'Letter of 75' case from 'Forcible seizure of power' to 'Obstruction of the exercise of electoral rights.' All defendants received a four-year sentence, suspended with two years of probation. This differs from the district court's verdict, which included property confiscation.

item.title: Azerbaijan International Bank acquires 51% stake in Uzbekistan's Davr Bank for $140 million
item.description: Azerbaijan International Bank (ABB) has purchased a 51% stake in the private Davr Bank for approximately $140 million. The transaction, valued at 1.646 trillion soms, occurred on the Tashkent Stock Exchange. This acquisition marks ABB's entry into the Uzbek banking market, as previously announced during a meeting between the presidents of Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Foreigner detained at Osh airport for alleged cigarette smuggling
item.description: A foreign national was detained at Osh International Airport on September 6 for allegedly smuggling a large batch of Esse Change cigarettes. The State Committee for National Security (GKNB) reported the incident. The suspect has been placed in pre-trial detention as an investigation is underway for economic smuggling. The GKNB is working to identify other potential participants in the scheme.

item.title: Uzbekistan aims to increase electrical engineering exports to $5 billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to boost its electrical engineering exports to $5 billion by 2030, according to a presentation reviewed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The sector's output has grown significantly, with exports already exceeding $1 billion to 65 countries. The strategy focuses on high-value products, including new items like electric vehicle charging stations and heat pumps.

item.title: Uzbekistan allocates $50 million for copper purchases by electrical engineering firms
item.description: Uzbekistan will allocate $50 million for electrical engineering companies to purchase copper raw materials. Firms will cover 25% of the cost, while 'UzSanoatExport' will finance the remaining 75%. This measure aims to support the growth and export potential of the country's electrical engineering sector.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan showcases investment opportunities at China's CIFIT fair
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Head of the National Investment Agency presented the country's investment potential and promising sectors at the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT) in Xiamen. The event aims to attract foreign capital and foster joint projects by connecting government agencies, businesses, and investors.

item.title: Young Kyrgyz citizens show higher digital financial literacy than older generations
item.description: A National Bank survey reveals young Kyrgyz citizens (18-29) exhibit higher digital financial literacy (56.9/100) than older individuals (60-79, 49.6/100). While the 30-59 age group scored highest overall (11.9/20), younger people demonstrated greater confidence in digital finance navigation and assessment.

item.title: Court reclassifies 'Letter of 75' case, sentences defendants to probation
item.description: Bishkek City Court reclassified the 'Letter of 75' case from attempting to seize power to obstructing electoral rights. Defendants, including former GKNB head Kamchybek Tashiev, received four-year sentences with two years of probation. The authors stated they did not intend to make Tashiev president or to cause conflict with Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Tashkent to experience planned water supply disruptions from September 14-22
item.description: Tashkent will face planned reductions or temporary shutdowns of drinking water supply across all districts from September 14 to October 22 due to maintenance on large water pipelines for the upcoming winter season. Water will be delivered by special vehicles to affected areas. A schedule is provided.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan establishes state enterprise for foreign student admissions
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has created a state enterprise, the Center for Admission of Foreign Students, to streamline and centralize the process. The initiative aims to increase transparency and attract more international applicants to the country's educational institutions. The center will manage recruitment, enrollment, and student support.

item.title: Defense to appeal Bishkek City Court's decision in 'Letter of 75' case
item.description: The defense team for former GKNB head Kamchybek Tashiev intends to appeal the Bishkek City Court's ruling in the 'Letter of 75' case. His lawyer stated the decision is illegal and unfounded, particularly regarding the reclassification of charges. The defendants disagree with the court's verdict and plan to appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Uzbekistan to change official currency exchange rate calculation from September 15
item.description: From September 15, Uzbekistan will alter its official currency exchange rate calculation method. The new system will consider transactions made on the interbank over-the-counter market alongside the exchange.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan 'Letters 75' case: all defendants receive probation, no charges of coup, no asset confiscation
item.description: Defendants in Kyrgyzstan's 'Letters 75' case have been sentenced to four years imprisonment with a two-year probation period. The charges do not include coup attempts, and there will be no confiscation of property.

item.title: Boghdod district to create over 240 new jobs through entrepreneurship development
item.description: The development of entrepreneurship in the Boghdod district is expected to create more than 240 new job opportunities. This initiative aims to boost local economic activity and employment.

item.title: Kazakhstan deputy proposes compensation for damage from low-quality gasoline
item.description: A deputy in Kazakhstan's parliament has proposed strengthening control over petroleum products and creating a compensation mechanism for citizens affected by low-quality fuel. He cited numerous complaints about AI-95 and AI-98 gasoline damaging vehicle parts. The proposal also includes random fuel sampling at gas stations and depots.

item.title: 'Letter of 75' case: Court reclassifies charge, imposes two-year probation
item.description: The Bishkek City Court has ruled on the 'Letter of 75' case, reclassifying the charge from 'violent seizure of power' to 'obstruction of electoral rights.' The previous district court ruling had sentenced several figures, including Kamchybek Tashiev, to four years imprisonment with probation. The new ruling does not include property confiscation.

item.title: Uzbek National Guard's core functions to be restructured for public safety
item.description: The core functions of Uzbekistan's National Guard are being restructured, consolidating tasks related to public safety and order. A new law requires National Guard officers to identify themselves when addressing citizens. The Senate has approved these changes.
